task: Plan horizon 10 of the agent-agnostic-browser-bridge project. Add a CDP-based scroll page action (scrollPage) to the tools/chrome-bridge package that materializes virtualized / lazy-rendered list rows the ISOLATED-world DOM-read path (readPage / getPageText / findElement) misses, shipped as one atomic page action end to end and reusing horizon 9's per-command chrome.debugger attach helper, verified by a live-Chrome head-to-head on a real virtualized list. Keep per-command attach/detach; do not touch the dead active-tab surface.

analysis.objective: Ship horizon 10 of agent-agnostic-browser-bridge: one atomic CDP-backed scroll page action in tools/chrome-bridge that materializes virtualized / lazy-rendered rows the ISOLATED-world DOM-read path (readPage/getPageText/findElement) misses, wired end to end and proven in live Chrome.
analysis.successDefinition: A single new page action (scrollPage, mirroring evaluatePage) lands across exactly the coordinated surface with no drift: PAGE_ACTIONS tuple entry (18->19), its Params + Result interfaces plus both PageActionParams / PageActionResults mapped-type entries in protocol/types.ts, a raw handler AND its guard()-wrapped entry in the Record<PageAction,Handler> maps in page-actions.ts, a TOOL_CATALOG Record<PageAction,ToolCatalogEntry> entry with honest description + inputSchema, both hardcoded action-count unit tests bumped to 19 (actions.unit.test.ts ordered-tuple + length, tool-catalog.unit.test.ts listTools length/label), and the README surface updated (count word 'eighteen'->'nineteen', '18 tools'->'19', both action enumerations, a prose paragraph, a manual e2e step). The handler resolves the sandbox tab via sandboxTab.resolveTabId() and drives it through a new DebuggerPorts method that reuses debugger-ports.ts withDebuggerSession (per-command chrome.debugger attach/detach, onDetach listener registered once at construction) issuing Input.dispatchMouseEvent wheel with a Runtime.evaluate scrollBy fallback - no persistent CDP session introduced. New exported symbols carry co-located unit tests (stubbed chrome global) per testguard; `npm run verify` in tools/chrome-bridge exits 0 (tsc --noEmit, eslint --max-warnings 0, vitest) with no skips/suppressions. The horizon closes only after a live-Chrome head-to-head in a fresh post-horizon-10 chrome-bridge MCP session against a real virtualized list, with a recorded transcript showing the scroll action causes a subsequent readPage to return row content that a readPage before the scroll did not; discoveries.md / state.md / blockers.md updated with the verdict, and decisions.md gets the binding choices (action name, scroll param model, event-dispatched vs rows-rendered success fidelity).
assumptions: Horizon 9 closed green (status.json: all 4 phases done, evaluatePage live-verified on github.com + reddit.com), so horizon 10 is a new capability, not a horizon-9 replan.

The action is one discrete MCP tool with a mirror-style name (scrollPage, paralleling evaluatePage), one-tool-per-action per the h1 decision, not an enum sub-mode.
Scroll targets the dedicated sandbox tab like every other action (resolveTabId), never the active/focused tab.
Params express a scroll intent narrowed to two optional fields (amountPx, toBottom); Result reports an observable signal (method, scrollY before/after, reachedEnd) rather than only 'dispatched'.

risks: CDP Input.dispatchMouseEvent wheel may not actually trigger a virtualized list's scroll listener / IntersectionObserver on an unfocused tab (same dispatched!=fired ceiling synthetic clickAt/hover hit on github/reddit); mitigated by the Runtime.evaluate scrollBy fallback, but if neither materializes rows phase 2 blocks and it is a REPLAN.
Lazy rows need render time after the scroll; no wait/settle action exists this horizon, so the live head-to-head needs manual delays and repeated scrollPage calls - making the proof timing-sensitive.

Per-command attach/detach means the scroll (CDP) and the confirming readPage (chrome.scripting) are separate sessions; a detach or SW suspension between them, or scroll position not persisting, could muddy the evidence.

phases.name: Add CDP scroll method to DebuggerPorts
phases.goal: Add a `scroll(tabId, intent)` method to the `DebuggerPorts` interface and its Chrome factory in `debugger-ports.ts` that moves the sandbox tab's scroll position over the Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP - the low-level `chrome.debugger` wire protocol), trying a synthetic mouse-wheel event first and falling back to a script scroll only when the wheel did not move the page, with full co-located unit tests.
phases.rationale: The bridge today has zero scroll capability: the ISOLATED-world `chrome.scripting` path used by `readPage`/`getPageText`/`findElement` cannot reliably move an unfocused tab's scroll position, so framework-virtualized rows (rows a UI only renders into the DOM once scrolled near the viewport) stay invisible to those reads. A CDP-issued scroll is the focus-independent, CSP-exempt motion that can materialize them, but a synthetic wheel event does not always drive scroll on a background tab, so the method needs a script fallback and must report which mechanism actually worked. This phase builds only the transport method so it can be reviewed in isolation before any action wiring.
changes: In `debugger-ports.ts`, add a third method to `interface DebuggerPorts`: `scroll(tabId: number, intent: ScrollIntent): Promise<ScrollOutcome>`. `ScrollIntent` carries EXACTLY two optional fields - `amountPx?: number` (pixels to scroll DOWN; scroll is always downward) and `toBottom?: boolean` (interpreted as ONE large downward jump toward the current bottom, using `document.documentElement.scrollHeight` as the target - NOT a loop that chases an infinite list; a caller that needs more calls the tool again). There is no `direction` field and no repeat count. When neither field is set, default to `amountPx = 2000` (roughly one large viewport). `ScrollOutcome` carries `{ readonly method: 'wheel' | 'script' | 'none'; readonly scrollYBefore: number; readonly scrollYAfter: number; readonly reachedEnd: boolean }` where `method` names the mechanism that actually moved the page (`'none'` if neither did) and `reachedEnd` is a BEST-EFFORT flag, `true` when `scrollYAfter + innerHeight >= scrollHeight - SLACK` (small pixel slack); on an infinite list that keeps growing it may read `false` forever, which is correct.

Implement the factory method by calling `withDebuggerSession(tabId, 'scrolling', run)` and widen the private label union type from `'capturing' | 'evaluating'` to `'capturing' | 'evaluating' | 'scrolling'` so the mid-command-detach rejection message reads `"...while scrolling"`. No persistent CDP session is introduced - this is one per-command attach/detach like every other method.

In `run`: (1) read `scrollY`/`scrollHeight`/`innerHeight`/`innerWidth` via `chrome.debugger.sendCommand({ tabId }, 'Runtime.evaluate', { expression, returnByValue: true, awaitPromise: true })` to get `scrollYBefore`; (2) issue `chrome.debugger.sendCommand({ tabId }, 'Input.dispatchMouseEvent', { type: 'mouseWheel', x, y, deltaX: 0, deltaY })` where `x`/`y` are pinned to the CENTRE of the visible viewport (`Math.round(innerWidth/2)`, `Math.round(innerHeight/2)` from step 1's read-back) so the wheel lands over page content, and `deltaY` is `amountPx` (or a large value covering `scrollHeight` when `toBottom`); (3) after a short fixed settle delay (a `Runtime.evaluate` of a ~150ms `await new Promise(r=>setTimeout(r,150))` - there is no wait/settle action this horizon) re-read `scrollY`; (4) if `scrollY` did not change from `scrollYBefore`, fall back to a second `Runtime.evaluate` running `window.scrollBy(0, amountPx)` (or `window.scrollTo(0, document.documentElement.scrollHeight)` when `toBottom`) and re-read `scrollY` again; (5) return `method: 'wheel'` if step 3 moved it, `'script'` if step 4 moved it, `'none'` otherwise - `method` names whichever mechanism produced the final observed movement - with the before/after `scrollY` and computed best-effort `reachedEnd`. Reuse the module-private `isRecord` helper to parse replies under `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`. Consult the CDP `Input.dispatchMouseEvent` reference so the `mouseWheel` param shape is correct, since the test asserts it byte-for-byte.

Add a `describe('scroll')` block to `debugger-ports.unit.test.ts` asserting: the exact `Input.dispatchMouseEvent`/`mouseWheel` command name and params; the wheel `x`/`y` being the viewport centre computed from the read-back; the exact `Runtime.evaluate` read-back and fallback params; `attach({tabId},'1.3')` then `detach` on both success and failure paths; re-attach after a failed command; the once-only `onDetach` listener; a mid-command detach that rejects carrying the `'scrolling'` label string; AND both mechanism paths explicitly - a wheel-only-success case (stub reports `scrollY` moved after the `Input.dispatchMouseEvent` call, so `Runtime.evaluate` scrollBy is NEVER sent and `method === 'wheel'`) and a wheel-then-script-fallback case (stub reports `scrollY` unchanged after the wheel, so the `window.scrollBy`/`scrollTo` `Runtime.evaluate` IS sent and `method === 'script'`). Name every new exported symbol (`ScrollIntent`, `ScrollOutcome`, any new helper) in the test per the testguard co-located-test rule.

PRE-DECLARED RIPPLE (the known trap from horizon 9's equivalent phase - adding a required interface method breaks every object literal typed as `DebuggerPorts`): update the two fake implementers so `tsc --noEmit` stays green - add a default `scroll: vi.fn(async () => ({ method: 'none' as const, scrollYBefore: 0, scrollYAfter: 0, reachedEnd: false }))` to the base object in `fakeDebugger(...)` in `page-actions.unit.test.ts`, and add a matching `scroll: () => Promise.resolve({ method: 'none' as const, scrollYBefore: 0, scrollYAfter: 0, reachedEnd: false })` entry to the literal returned by `fakeDebuggerPorts()` (around line 87) in `service-worker.unit.test.ts`. No `service-worker.ts` source change is needed - `pageActionHandlers` already receives `deps.debuggerPorts`.

rubric.ruleStatement: The DebuggerPorts interface gains exactly one new method scroll(tabId: number, intent: ScrollIntent): Promise<ScrollOutcome>, with ScrollIntent carrying only amountPx?: number and toBottom?: boolean, and ScrollOutcome being a readonly { method: 'wheel' | 'script' | 'none'; scrollYBefore: number; scrollYAfter: number; reachedEnd: boolean }. 10 = exact shape plus the amountPx default and toBottom single-jump semantics implemented at the right layer; 8 = shape correct and defaults applied; below minScore = extra fields or a widened method type.
passCriteria: interface DebuggerPorts declares scroll with the exact signature and no other new members
ScrollIntent has exactly two optional fields amountPx and toBottom - no direction, no repeat/count/times
ScrollOutcome has exactly the four readonly fields with method literally 'wheel' | 'script' | 'none'
ScrollIntent and ScrollOutcome are exported and each named in debugger-ports.unit.test.ts
amountPx default 2000 applied in the factory implementation (not left undefined at the wire call); toBottom targets document.documentElement.scrollHeight as a single jump, not a loop
failureExamples: A careful dev adds direction?: 'up' | 'down' 'for symmetry' or a repeat?: number field - extra surface the phase explicitly cut
ScrollOutcome.method typed as string, or reachedEnd omitted, or fields not marked readonly
amountPx default of 2000 implemented as a JS default parameter on a nested helper that the toBottom branch bypasses, so toBottom + omitted amountPx sends deltaY: NaN
scroll added only to the Chrome factory object and not to the interface, so fakes typed as DebuggerPorts still compile without it

rubric.label: Exact CDP command names and params asserted in tests
rubric.ruleStatement: The unit tests assert the literal CDP wire calls: Input.dispatchMouseEvent with type 'mouseWheel' and correct param keys, the Runtime.evaluate read-backs/fallback, and the wheel x/y being the viewport centre computed from the read-back. 10 = every param pinned and x/y proven derived from the read-back; 8 = command names + key params pinned; below minScore = objectContaining stubs that never pin mouseWheel or deltaY.
passCriteria: a test asserts sendCommand called with method 'Input.dispatchMouseEvent' and params containing type: 'mouseWheel', x, y, deltaX: 0, deltaY
a test asserts x === Math.round(innerWidth/2) and y === Math.round(innerHeight/2) using values fed by the stubbed first Runtime.evaluate read-back (not hardcoded)
deltaY asserted to equal the resolved amountPx (default 2000) on the default path and a scrollHeight-covering value on toBottom
the read-back Runtime.evaluate asserted with returnByValue: true and awaitPromise: true; the settle delay is a Runtime.evaluate of a setTimeout promise (no wall-clock sleep in the test)
the fallback Runtime.evaluate expression asserted to be window.scrollBy(0, amountPx) default / window.scrollTo(0, document.documentElement.scrollHeight) on toBottom
failureExamples: tests assert only expect.objectContaining({}) and never pin type: 'mouseWheel' or deltaY, so a wrong delta sign or missing mouseWheel type passes
a diligent dev pins x/y to literal numbers (640/360) matching the stub fixture instead of asserting they are derived from the read-back
the test asserts Input.dispatchMouseEvent params but the implementation omits deltaX and Chrome would reject it - lenient stub does not model required params
fallback assertion checks 'scrollBy' substring only, so window.scrollBy(0, 0) or a swapped-axis call still passes

rubric.label: Attach/detach cleanup and label union on every path
rubric.ruleStatement: scroll() runs entirely inside withDebuggerSession(tabId, 'scrolling', run) with per-command attach then detach on both success and failure, no persistent session, and the private label union widened to include 'scrolling'. 10 = all CDP work inside run, no new persistent attach state anywhere, mid-detach message asserts 'scrolling'; 8 = withDebuggerSession reused and detach covered on both paths; below minScore = attach/detach open-coded or a session cached across the wheel/fallback boundary.
passCriteria: the factory scroll method calls withDebuggerSession with the literal label 'scrolling' and does all CDP work inside run
the label union type is widened to include 'scrolling'
a test asserts attach({tabId}, '1.3') then detach on the success path, and detach still runs when a sendCommand rejects
a test asserts re-attach works after a failed command and the onDetach listener is registered once only
a test asserts a mid-command detach rejects with a message containing 'scrolling'
no module-level or instance-level CDP session/attach state is added outside withDebuggerSession
failureExamples: the dev calls chrome.debugger.attach/detach directly inside scroll instead of reusing withDebuggerSession, diverging on the error-path detach
withDebuggerSession is used but the settle-delay Runtime.evaluate is awaited outside the run callback, so on a slow page detach fires before the second read-back
label union widened and 'scrolling' passed, but the mid-command-detach rejection message is built from a shared constant that still says 'evaluating'
a caching optimization keeps the debugger attached between the wheel call and the fallback across a helper boundary, leaving the session attached if the fallback throws

rubric.label: Wheel-first, script-fallback branch logic with honest method reporting
rubric.ruleStatement: The implementation tries the synthetic wheel first, re-reads scrollY after a settle, and only issues the window.scrollBy/scrollTo Runtime.evaluate when scrollY did not change; method reflects whichever mechanism actually produced the final observed movement ('none' if neither did). 10 = three explicit tests (wheel-only, fallback, neither) plus tolerant float comparison and reachedEnd both-cases; 8 = wheel-only and fallback tests pass with honest method; below minScore = both mechanisms always fired or method set on command-resolved not page-moved.
passCriteria: a wheel-only-success test: stub reports scrollY moved after Input.dispatchMouseEvent, so the fallback Runtime.evaluate is NEVER sent and method === 'wheel'
a wheel-then-script-fallback test: stub reports scrollY unchanged after the wheel, the fallback IS sent, and method === 'script'
a neither-moved test: both mechanisms leave scrollY unchanged and method === 'none'
scrollYBefore/scrollYAfter are the actual first and final read-back values
reachedEnd computed as scrollYAfter + innerHeight >= scrollHeight - SLACK with a small constant slack, and a test covers both true and false
failureExamples: the dev always sends both the wheel and the scrollBy for robustness and reports method based on which delta is larger - the wheel-only test fails because the fallback evaluate was still sent
fallback is gated on scrollYAfter === scrollYBefore using strict equality on floats; a sub-pixel wheel movement is treated as 'no movement' and the script path runs unnecessarily
method is set to 'wheel' whenever the wheel command resolved without throwing, regardless of movement, so a dispatched-but-inert wheel on a background tab is reported as success
reachedEnd uses scrollHeight - scrollYAfter <= innerHeight without slack, so a list with 1px sub-pixel rounding never reports reachedEnd at the true bottom

rubric.label: CDP reply parsing via isRecord under strict TS, no unsafe casts
rubric.ruleStatement: Runtime.evaluate replies are narrowed through isRecord (or equivalent) with no any, no non-null assertions, no `as T` on JSON-value results, tolerating a malformed/empty reply without throwing. 10 = degenerate-reply test asserts method: 'none' and numeric guards reject NaN; 8 = isRecord used and no banned syntax; below minScore = `as { result: { value: number } }` casts against the stub.
passCriteria: scrollY/scrollHeight/innerHeight/innerWidth extracted via isRecord checks and numeric guards, not result.result.value as number
no new occurrences of `any`, `!`, or `... as <type>` on a sendCommand reply in the scroll code path
a test covers a degenerate reply (missing result field or non-numeric value) and asserts scroll resolves with method: 'none' rather than rejecting
the settle-delay evaluate result is not parsed for a value it does not need
isRecord is imported/used rather than re-implemented
failureExamples: const y = (reply as { result: { value: number } }).result.value - works against the stub, banned by no-restricted-syntax, unsafe against a real malformed reply

phases.healerHint: The most likely miss is the wheel-then-script branch: the executor sends both the Input.dispatchMouseEvent wheel and the window.scrollBy fallback unconditionally (or gates the fallback on strict float equality of scrollY), breaking the wheel-only-success test and the honest method reporting - gate the fallback on an observed no-movement re-read with small pixel tolerance and only then set method to 'script'.

phases.name: Add scrollPage page action across the parity surface
phases.goal: Wire a new `scrollPage` page action end to end through the six coordinated places every bridge action must appear, bump both hardcoded action-count unit tests from 18 to 19, and update the README count/enumeration/prose/manual-e2e surface - so the MCP server advertises `scrollPage` as a discrete tool with a two-field input schema and the extension handler drives the sandbox tab through `DebuggerPorts.scroll`.
phases.rationale: The bridge keeps its action set drift-free by forcing each action to appear in a fixed set of `Record<PageAction, ...>`-typed locations (an omission becomes a `tsc` error) plus two hardcoded count tests and the README. `scrollPage` (named to mirror the existing `evaluatePage`, one discrete MCP tool, not an enum sub-mode) must land in all of them in one reviewable change. The handler resolves the dedicated unfocused sandbox tab and calls the transport method built in phase 0.
changes: In `actions.ts`, append `'scrollPage'` to the `PAGE_ACTIONS` `as const` tuple (after `getTabState`, the end - a scroll action has no natural neighbor, so appending is lowest-risk), taking the length from 18 to 19. No other change: `PageAction`, `isPageAction` derive generically.

In `types.ts`, add `ScrollPageParams` with EXACTLY two optional readonly fields - `amountPx?: number` (pixels to scroll down; default 2000 when omitted) and `toBottom?: boolean` (one large downward jump toward the current bottom, not a loop) - and `ScrollPageResult` (readonly: `method: 'wheel' | 'script' | 'none'`, `scrollYBefore: number`, `scrollYAfter: number`, `reachedEnd: boolean`; build it without ever assigning `undefined` explicitly because `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` is on). Add one key each to the `PageActionParams` and `PageActionResults` mapped types. There is no `direction` and no `repeat`/`count` field.

In `page-actions.ts`, add a `scrollPage` entry to BOTH the raw `Record<PageAction, Handler>` object and the `guard(...)`-wrapped return map. The handler: validate params (each present field must be the right type - `amountPx` a non-negative finite number, `toBottom` a boolean) and return a plain `{ error: 'scrollPage accepts an optional numeric amountPx and an optional boolean toBottom' }` sentinel BEFORE calling anything (h9's test asserts the port is not called on bad params), THEN `const tabId = await sandboxTab.resolveTabId()`, THEN build the `ScrollIntent` (omit fields not supplied; do not default in the handler - the port defaults `amountPx` to 2000) and `await captureDebugger.scroll(tabId, intent)`, then coerce to a JSON-safe `{ result: { method, scrollYBefore, scrollYAfter, reachedEnd } }` via a NEW small dedicated coercer written in the `coercePointerOutcome` style (do NOT reuse `InPageScriptOutcome`/`coerceExecuteScriptOutcome` - the scroll outcome is a status object, not an evaluated JSON value). Name the new coercer and any helper in the co-located test.

In `tool-catalog.ts`, add a `scrollPage` entry to the `TOOL_CATALOG` `Record<PageAction, ToolCatalogEntry>` with an honest description (names the CDP `Input.dispatchMouseEvent` wheel attempt and the `Runtime.evaluate` `window.scrollBy`/`scrollTo` fallback, states it targets the sandbox tab, states the purpose is materializing virtualized/lazy-rendered rows the ISOLATED-world reads miss, and that the result reports which mechanism moved the page) and an `inputSchema` with EXACTLY two optional properties: `amountPx` (`{ type: 'number', minimum: 0 }`, described as pixels to scroll down, default 2000) and `toBottom` (`{ type: 'boolean' }`), `required: []`, `additionalProperties: false`. Add a reusable `SCROLL_PROPERTIES` `as const` block alongside the existing shared property consts. `listTools()` needs no change.
In `actions.unit.test.ts`, add `'scrollPage'` to the ordered-tuple `toEqual([...])` assertion and change `PAGE_ACTIONS.length` `.toBe(18)` to `.toBe(19)`.

In `tool-catalog.unit.test.ts`, change `listTools()` `.toHaveLength(18)` to `19`, change the `it('advertises exactly eighteen tools', ...)` label to `'nineteen'`, add `scrollPage` to the required-map assertion, and add a schema-shape test asserting the scroll `inputSchema` exposes only `amountPx` and `toBottom` with no required fields.

In `README.md`: line ~48 `'eighteen'`->`'nineteen'` and add `scrollPage` to the inline enumeration (lines ~48-53); line ~177 `'18 tools'`->`'19'`; add `scrollPage` to the second full enumeration in the built `service-worker.js` bullet (lines ~205-211); add a `scrollPage` prose paragraph mirroring the `evaluatePage` one that describes the two-field param model (`amountPx` default 2000, `toBottom`) and the wheel-then-script fallback with the `method` field in the result; add a new numbered manual-e2e step (step 14) for a virtualized-list scroll head-to-head, following h9's step-12 template (numbered step + a dated `Verified ...` paragraph left as a stub for phase 2).

If any file touched in this phase contains a stale action-count comment (e.g. `types.ts` line ~10 'the ten generic page actions', `tool-catalog.ts` line ~4 'Two of the ten tools'), fix it in passing since the file is already open; do not go hunting in untouched files like `server.ts`.

phases.name: Verify scrollPage in live Chrome against a virtualized list
phases.goal: In a fresh chrome-bridge MCP session started after a full rebuild and extension reload, run a live-Chrome head-to-head on a named public virtualized list proving that `scrollPage` causes a subsequent `readPage` to return row content that a `readPage` before the scroll did not, and record the dated transcript and the binding h10 decisions in the roadmap memory files.
phases.rationale: The horizon's only closure gate is empirical: synthetic input dispatch has repeatedly hit a 'dispatched but the page's listener never fired' ceiling in this project, so `scrollPage` is not proven until a transcript shows it actually materialized otherwise-absent DOM rows and shows which mechanism (`wheel` or `script`) did it. This check has stalled in prior horizons purely because of stale MCP/extension builds, so the rebuild and fresh-session steps are explicit here.
changes: Rebuild `dist/extension` in `tools/chrome-bridge`, restart the MCP server, then remove and re-add the unpacked extension in `chrome://extensions` (a stale service worker manifests as a silent command timeout). Start a NEW chrome-bridge MCP session AFTER the rebuild so it advertises the `scrollPage` tool.

PRIMARY verification target (do not substitute at executor discretion): the TanStack Virtual React `Infinite Scroll` example at `https://tanstack.com/virtual/latest/docs/framework/react/examples/infinite-scroll` - a public, no-auth, windowed list that renders only near-viewport rows into the DOM. BACKUP target if the primary will not load or does not withhold rows in a backgrounded tab: the react-window fixed-size-list demo at `https://react-window.vercel.app/#/examples/list/fixed-size`. Before the head-to-head, do a quick sanity check ON THE NAMED PAGE confirming BOTH that the virtualized list lives in the MAIN document (not an embedded demo iframe - `readPage` and `scrollPage` act on the top-level document, so an iframe-hosted list would never be touched) AND that an at-rest `readPage` withholds off-screen rows that appear after a manual scroll. If the primary target hosts its list in an iframe or does not withhold rows in a backgrounded tab, switch to the backup; if neither passes, pick another public main-document infinite-scroll list and name it in the transcript.

Empirically resolve, against the named page, whether CDP `Input.dispatchMouseEvent` `mouseWheel` to the unfocused sandbox tab drives scroll and fires the list's scroll/IntersectionObserver listeners (the `scrollPage` result's `method` field will read `'wheel'`), versus the `window.scrollBy`/`scrollTo` fallback doing it (`method: 'script'`), versus neither (`method: 'none'`).

Run the head-to-head via the MCP session: `navigateTo` the chosen URL, `readPage` (capture row set A), `scrollPage` REPEATEDLY (2-5 calls with a large `amountPx` or `toBottom: true`, pausing between calls for lazy rows to render - one scroll is not expected to be enough on an infinite list), `readPage` again (capture row set B), and confirm B contains rows absent from A. Paste the real transcript, with the date and the observed `method` value, into README manual-e2e step 14's `Verified <date> (horizon 10)` paragraph.

On a real pass: record the verdict in `docs/roadmaps/.../discoveries.md` and `state.md`; in `docs/roadmaps/.../decisions.md` add the h10 line with the binding choices: action name `scrollPage`; the narrowed two-field param model (`amountPx` optional, default 2000; `toBottom` optional boolean; no `direction`, no repeat count); and the success-fidelity choice (result reports `method: 'wheel' | 'script' | 'none'` plus before/after `scrollY` and `reachedEnd`, i.e. mechanism-that-moved-the-page fidelity, not bare event-dispatched). Note persistent CDP session stays out of scope. Mark `tools/chrome-bridge/blockers.md` item 2 ('No scroll primitive') resolved, note item 7's partial dependency, and update `docs/roadmaps/.../blockers.md` with the outcome.

NO PENDING-MARKER COMPLETION: if the fresh MCP session cannot be established, or the extension build is stale and unfixable in-session, or no named target materializes rows, this phase ends BLOCKED - write `MANUAL_CHROME_CHECK_PENDING` into the ledger / `state.md` / `discoveries.md` with the exact rebuild, reload, fresh-session, and target-URL steps a follow-up must run, and the horizon stays OPEN. A pending marker is a blocked state, never a completed phase; do not mark this phase done on a pending marker.

h9 roadmap phase 4 shape (rebuild -> restart -> remove+re-add unpacked extension -> fresh MCP session -> record transcript)
phases.expectedResult: README manual-e2e step 14 carries a real dated `Verified <date> (horizon 10)` before/after transcript showing `scrollPage` revealed rows a prior `readPage` missed on the named TanStack Virtual page (or the named backup), including the observed `method` value; `decisions.md` has the h10 line (action name, two-field param model, mechanism-fidelity result); and `discoveries.md`, `state.md`, `blockers.md`, and `tools/chrome-bridge/blockers.md` record the verdict. If verification could not be completed, the phase ends BLOCKED with a `MANUAL_CHROME_CHECK_PENDING` marker and reproduction steps, and the horizon stays OPEN.
phases.compensation: None - this phase only reads live Chrome and writes documentation; a wrong verdict is corrected by re-running the check in a new session.

rubric.label: Real dated before/after transcript in README step 14
rubric.ruleStatement: README manual-e2e step 14 must carry an actual, dated live-Chrome transcript - literal pasted tool output, not a narrative summary - that shows both readPage calls and the row delta. 10 = both readPage outputs pasted verbatim, a named delta row, scrollPage result JSON, and the method value all present; 8 = both reads pasted and delta identifiable; below minScore = a plausible-sounding prose write-up with no pasted output.
passCriteria: A Verified <date> (horizon 10) paragraph exists under README manual-e2e step 14 with a concrete calendar date, not a placeholder or <date> token
The transcript shows readPage result A (pre-scroll) AND readPage result B (post-scroll) as pasted output blocks, not paraphrased
At least one specific delta row (present in B, absent from A) is called out by its identifying text or index
The intervening scrollPage calls are shown, including their JSON results
The observed method value is stated explicitly as one of wheel | script | none
The named target URL appears verbatim in the transcript
failureExamples: The paragraph reads 'Verified that scrollPage revealed 25 additional rows that readPage did not show before scrolling' with a date but no pasted readPage output - a plausible-looking write-up that cannot be audited
Transcript pastes readPage B and the scrollPage results but only says 'readPage before showed fewer rows' for A without pasting it
method is described as 'the wheel path worked' in prose but the actual scrollPage result JSON showing "method":"wheel" is not pasted
Date matches the session date but the transcript content is templated from the h9 step-12 example rather than a fresh run

rubric.label: Main-document (not iframe) pre-check actually performed
rubric.ruleStatement: The deliverable must show the named virtualized list was confirmed to live in the top-level document (not an embedded demo iframe) before the head-to-head, because readPage/scrollPage only act on the main document. 10 = the check is recorded with the evidence used and the row-withholding sanity check for the same page; 8 = a recorded main-document check on the chosen page; below minScore = documentation-knowledge assertion with no observed check.
passCriteria: The transcript or memory-file notes record an explicit check that the list is in the main document, with the evidence used (readPage returned the list rows at top level, or a frame inspection showing no wrapping iframe)
The check is performed against the SAME named page used for the head-to-head
If the primary TanStack target was found to be iframe-hosted, the switch to the backup (or another named main-document list) is recorded with that reason
The at-rest row-withholding sanity check is also recorded for the chosen page
failureExamples: The write-up states 'the TanStack Virtual infinite-scroll example is a windowed list' and proceeds, without any recorded check of whether the live example page wraps it in an iframe
The pre-check is done on the react-window demo but the head-to-head is actually run on the TanStack page
Row-withholding is asserted from documentation knowledge of virtualization rather than an observed readPage-vs-manual-scroll comparison on the page

rubric.label: Fresh post-rebuild MCP session evidenced
rubric.ruleStatement: The transcript must show the head-to-head ran in a chrome-bridge MCP session started AFTER a full dist/extension rebuild + extension remove/re-add, since stale builds have silently stalled this gate before. 10 = rebuild, server restart, remove+re-add, and a tool-listing or post-phase-1-only call all recorded in order; 8 = rebuild + re-add recorded before the first head-to-head call; below minScore = 'ran against the running bridge' with no rebuild evidence.
passCriteria: The deliverable records the rebuild of dist/extension in tools/chrome-bridge and the MCP server restart, in order
The extension remove-and-re-add in chrome://extensions is recorded (not just a reload)
Evidence the new session advertises scrollPage as a tool (a tool listing, or a successful scrollPage call that could only work post-phase-1)
The ordering is unambiguous: rebuild/reload precede the first navigateTo/readPage of the head-to-head
failureExamples: The write-up says 'ran against the running bridge' and shows a working scrollPage call, but never states that a rebuild + extension re-add happened first
Rebuild is mentioned but only reloadTab / service-worker reload is recorded, not the full remove+re-add
scrollPage calls succeed but there is no evidence the session post-dates phase 1's build

rubric.label: decisions.md carries the h10 binding line
rubric.ruleStatement: decisions.md must gain an h10 entry recording the three binding choices: the action name, the two-field param model, and the mechanism-fidelity result shape. 10 = all three plus the explicit no-direction/no-repeat cut and the persistent-session-out-of-scope note; 8 = action name + param model + fidelity; below minScore = an outcome line that omits the param-model and fidelity bindings.
passCriteria: An h10-labeled entry exists in docs/roadmaps/agent-agnostic-browser-bridge/decisions.md
It states the action name scrollPage
It states the narrowed param model: amountPx optional (default 2000), toBottom optional boolean, and explicitly that there is no direction and no repeat/count field
It states the success-fidelity choice: result reports method: 'wheel' | 'script' | 'none' plus before/after scrollY and reachedEnd
It notes persistent CDP session stays out of scope
failureExamples: decisions.md gets 'h10: added scrollPage action, verified in live Chrome' - records the outcome but omits the param-model and fidelity bindings a future horizon needs
The entry lists amountPx and toBottom but does not state that direction and repeat-count were deliberately cut
The mechanism-fidelity decision is written in discoveries.md but not in decisions.md

rubric.label: Memory files updated with the verdict, consistently
rubric.ruleStatement: discoveries.md, state.md, blockers.md, and tools/chrome-bridge/blockers.md must all record the h10 outcome consistently with the README transcript. 10 = all four updated, item 2 resolved with item 7 dependency noted, zero contradictions; 8 = all four updated consistently; below minScore = a blockers.md left stale or a state/blockers contradiction.
passCriteria: discoveries.md records the empirical verdict (wheel, script, or neither materialized rows on the named page) with the date, one line
state.md reflects horizon 10 status consistent with the phase result (done only if a real pass; open if blocked)
docs/roadmaps/agent-agnostic-browser-bridge/blockers.md updated with the outcome
tools/chrome-bridge/blockers.md item 2 ('No scroll primitive') marked resolved on a pass, with item 7's partial dependency noted
No contradiction between files
failureExamples: discoveries.md and state.md are updated but both blockers.md files are left untouched, so item 2 still reads 'No scroll primitive' after the capability shipped
state.md is marked 'horizon 10 complete' while the README transcript paragraph is still a stub
The verdict recorded in discoveries.md ('method: script') contradicts the README transcript ('method: wheel')

rubric.label: Pending marker treated as BLOCKED, never as a pass
rubric.ruleStatement: If verification could not be completed, the deliverable must record a MANUAL_CHROME_CHECK_PENDING marker as a BLOCKED state with exact reproduction steps and the horizon left OPEN - and must NOT present the phase as done. 10 = marker only when a real transcript is absent, with rebuild + remove/re-add + fresh-session + target URLs spelled out, and status shows OPEN/BLOCKED; below minScore = a pending marker laundered into a phase-done / horizon-closed status.
passCriteria: If and only if a real transcript is absent, the ledger / state.md / discoveries.md carry MANUAL_CHROME_CHECK_PENDING
The marker is accompanied by exact steps: rebuild command, extension remove/re-add, fresh-session start, and the specific target URL(s)
state.md and any status file show horizon 10 as OPEN / phase as BLOCKED - not complete, not passed
No memory file claims the scroll primitive is verified or blocker item 2 is resolved while the marker is present
Conversely, if a real dated transcript IS present, no stale pending marker is left in the files
failureExamples: The phase hits a stale-build wall, writes 'MANUAL_CHROME_CHECK_PENDING - retry later' into state.md, and the same commit marks the phase status done / horizon closed
Pending marker is written but with only a vague 'rebuild and retry' note, missing the target URLs and the remove/re-add step
blockers.md item 2 is marked resolved 'pending final live check' even though no transcript exists
A real run succeeded but an earlier MANUAL_CHROME_CHECK_PENDING line was never removed from discoveries.md

phases.healerHint: Paste the literal readPage-A / scrollPage / readPage-B tool output with a real date, the named URL, the main-document (non-iframe) pre-check, evidence of a post-rebuild fresh MCP session, and the observed method value into README step 14; mirror the verdict into decisions.md (h10 binding line), discoveries.md, state.md, and both blockers.md files - and if any of that is missing, write MANUAL_CHROME_CHECK_PENDING with exact repro steps and leave the horizon OPEN rather than marking the phase done.

successCriteria: A single new page action (scrollPage) lands across exactly the coordinated surface with no drift (PAGE_ACTIONS 18->19, Params+Result interfaces + both mapped types, raw + guarded handler entries, TOOL_CATALOG entry, both hardcoded action-count unit tests bumped to 19, README count/enumerations/prose/manual-e2e step), driven by a new DebuggerPorts.scroll method reusing withDebuggerSession per-command attach/detach with no persistent CDP session; npm run verify in tools/chrome-bridge exits 0 with no skips/suppressions; and the horizon closes only after a live-Chrome head-to-head transcript shows scrollPage causes a subsequent readPage to return rows a prior readPage did not.

Add CDP scroll method to DebuggerPorts: DebuggerPorts.scroll(tabId, intent) exists with a two-field ScrollIntent and a method-bearing ScrollOutcome, implemented via withDebuggerSession(..., 'scrolling', ...) as a wheel-then-script fallback with no persistent session, with a describe('scroll') unit-test block covering both mechanism paths and the two test fakes updated; npm run verify green.

Add scrollPage page action across the parity surface: scrollPage present in PAGE_ACTIONS (19), both mapped types, both handler maps, TOOL_CATALOG (schema exposes only amountPx + toBottom), both count tests (19), and the README (both enumerations, count word, prose paragraph, manual-e2e step 14 stub); npm run verify green with no skips.

Verify scrollPage in live Chrome against a virtualized list: README manual-e2e step 14 carries a real dated before/after transcript showing scrollPage revealed rows a prior readPage missed on a named main-document virtualized list including the observed method value; decisions.md has the h10 binding line; discoveries.md/state.md/blockers.md and tools/chrome-bridge/blockers.md record the verdict - OR the phase ends BLOCKED with a MANUAL_CHROME_CHECK_PENDING marker and exact reproduction steps and the horizon stays OPEN.
deferred: Trusted keyboard input via CDP Input.dispatchKeyEvent - a separate deferred capability slice; scoping picked scroll over trusted keyboard, and bundling both would make the horizon a family the brief forbids.
Trusted click-by-coordinate via CDP Input.dispatchMouseEvent press/release - different slice; held for a later horizon.
A wait/settle action - not the chosen slice; scroll verification uses manual delays this horizon, and a first-class wait/settle action is its own horizon (and a strong horizon 11 candidate).
Moving to a persistent multi-command CDP session - scoping explicitly keeps per-command attach/detach; deferred until a slice needs ordered Input.dispatch* sequencing.
Deleting or altering the dead active-tab surface (queryActiveTab / captureVisibleTab / activeTab permission / NO_ACTIVE_TAB) - the user chose to leave it untouched this horizon.
Resurrecting horizon 5's DOM page-model snapshot (ref-addressable rows + bounding boxes) - a separate never-executed roadmap; scroll does not require it.
Switching readPage / getPageText / findElement to a CDP evaluation path - they stay on chrome.scripting ISOLATED world; only the scroll motion uses CDP.
A distinct scroll-element-into-view-by-selector action - the horizon ships ONE atomic scroll action; a selector-targeted variant is additional surface.
Cleaning up stale action-count comments outside files touched by phase 1 (server.ts headers) - only touched-in-passing fixes are in scope; a dedicated cleanup is deferred (5th time).
Verifying the MCP config against Gemini CLI / Codex CLI / Cursor - h4 decision binds hand-verification to Claude Code only.
Wiring tools/chrome-bridge into the repo-root verify.sh pipeline - h1 decision keeps the package self-contained.
A direction param and a repeat/count field on the scroll action - cut by the user redirect; scrollPage is always downward and a caller needing more scrolling calls the tool again.
